title: Base change of a Noetherian local algebra along a finite purely inseparable extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $k'/k$ a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] and $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a $k$-algebra. Put $A'=A\otimes_kk'$, an $A$-algebra via $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. Then: (1) $A'$ is a free $A$-module of rank $[k':k]$, in particular $A\to A'$ is finite and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $A'$ is Noetherian; (2) $A'$ is a local ring, and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ is the only prime ideal of $A'$ containing $\mathfrak mA'$; (3) the residue field $K'=A'/\mathfrak m'$ is a finite field extension of $K$, and $A'/\mathfrak mA'\cong K\otimes_kk'$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular, line 8697), proof of (3) => (1) (lines 8716-8750): 'Set A' = A (x)_k k'. This is a local ring with maximal ideal m' ... since A -> A' is finite flat'; stated there without proof
